whatIsThis.heading: What is this?
whatIsThis.body: UN Transcripts is a public preview tool that automatically generates transcripts from public United Nations meeting recordings, for example <webtvLink>UN Web TV</webtvLink>. These transcripts are not official UN records.

whoIsItFor.heading: Who is it for?
whoIsItFor.intro: The tool is designed to help anyone who needs quick access to the spoken content of public UN meetings, including:
whoIsItFor.item1: Diplomats and delegation staff following proceedings across multiple organs
whoIsItFor.item2: Researchers and academics studying public UN debates and voting records
whoIsItFor.item4: Civil society organisations engaging in policy discussions
whoIsItFor.item5: UN Secretariat staff reviewing public meeting records

coverage.heading: What meetings are covered?
coverage.intro: The tool covers public meetings recorded and published on public UN platforms, including:
coverage.item5: Other inter-governmental bodies as available on UN Web TV
coverage.closed: Closed or confidential meetings are not recorded on Web TV and are therefore not covered.

howItWorks.heading: How it works
howItWorks.step1Body: The system keeps an always up-to-date collection of UN meetings via UN Web TV.
howItWorks.step2Body: We transcribe the existing UN audio channels — the original "floor" channel and each of the available official UN interpretation channels. No machine translation is applied. Each channel is transcribed by an appropriate speech-to-text model for that language.
howItWorks.step3Body: After transcription, a second model analyses the text and audio to assign names and affiliations to each speaker where possible. It uses contextual clues — such as the chair introducing delegates, country name mentions, and speaker diarization — together with the official list of participants when available. Where this is not possible, placeholders such as “Speaker 1” are displayed.
howItWorks.step4Body: The transcript is automatically analysed to identify the main policy topics discussed, using categories relevant to the proceedings (e.g. humanitarian affairs, international peace and security, human rights). The defined topics depend on the content of each video, and do not follow a pre-defined schema. They are for informational purposes only.
howItWorks.step5Body: Where official <pvLink>verbatim records (procès-verbaux, or PVs)</pvLink> or <srLink>summary records (SR documents)</srLink> exist, the site also makes them available alongside the unofficial automatic transcripts.

models.heading: Transcription model per language
models.intro: Different speech-to-text providers excel at different languages, so each track is routed to the model that performs best for it in our evaluation.
models.postProcessing: Post-processing — speaker identification and topic classification — is performed by Azure OpenAI GPT-5.5 for all languages.

accuracy.heading: Accuracy and limitations
accuracy.para1: These transcripts are created using automatic speech recognition and are not official records.
accuracy.para2: They are a faster, unofficial reference, but should not be cited as authoritative. For the official record, please refer to the <odsLink>UN Official Document System</odsLink> (verbatim records, summary records, and resolutions).
accuracy.issuesIntro: Automatic transcription is much faster than human transcription but may introduce errors. Common issues include:
accuracy.issue1: Names, abbreviations or document symbols may be misheard or misspelt
accuracy.issue2: Accuracy can also vary by speaker and microphone quality
accuracy.issue3: For very long meetings, not all speakers may be distinguished

sources.heading: Data sources
sources.webtvBody: — Meeting recordings and metadata, delivered via the platform (publicly accessible at webtv.un.org).
sources.odsBody: — Official verbatim records (PV documents) retrieved from documents.un.org where available.

api.heading: Using this programmatically
api.intro: Every meeting page has a matching data endpoint — append .json for structured data, or .txt for plain text, compact enough to use as LLM context.
api.search: To search or list meetings across the archive, fetch /{locale}/meetings.json — filter with ?date=, ?q=, ?category=, or ?from=/?to= for a date range. Add ?ft=1 to a query to also search inside the transcripts themselves — matched meetings then include the matching statements, each with a link to the exact moment in the meeting.

forAgents.heading: For AI agents
forAgents.body: If you are an LLM or autonomous agent, start at <llmsLink>llms.txt</llmsLink> for a structured guide to this API — the URL grammar, the search endpoint, and a recommended fetch workflow. A full machine-readable schema is available as an <openapiLink>OpenAPI reference</openapiLink>.
